item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02650","case1_error":"Counts only two houses in the combined total, although Zion and his two friends built three.","case2_error":"Labels the soda consumed and given away as soda remaining, instead of subtracting it from three bottles.","reason":"The first omits a contributor; the second confuses the amount removed with the amount remaining.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02651","case1_error":"Evaluates 30 + 35 + 46 as 101 instead of 111.","case2_error":"Omits subtracting the 30 oranges reserved for juice, yielding 250 instead of 220.","reason":"The first incorrectly evaluates a correctly written expression; the second leaves a required deduction out of its expression.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02652","case1_error":"Gives unsupported 74; the distance-and-time plan lacks required data. An arithmetic mean interpretation gives 40.","case2_error":"Writes correct formulas but supplies unexplained numerical answers, none equal to the correct $79.","reason":"The coaster question materially ambiguously specifies average speed: an arithmetic mean determines the answer, whereas a time-weighted average requires missing durations.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02653","case1_error":"Adds brownies given to Carl and Simon and reports that sum as brownies remaining.","case2_error":"Incorrectly converts half a ton to 500 pounds, then reports 15 bags without support from its formulas.","reason":"The first confuses amounts given away with the remainder; the second contains an incorrect unit conversion and an unsupported final number.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02654","case1_error":"Divides the retained 80% volume by loss per jump, then unjustifiably subtracts that jump count from itself.","case2_error":"Evaluates (1/4) × 3 × 14 as 14 instead of 10.5, inflating the total.","reason":"The first uses erroneous relations to calculate jumps; the second makes a numerical evaluation error in a correctly written expression.","judgment":"different"}]}
